column1: # Z8: what each file of upstream's zenoh/tests must still do against the patched graph.
# Graded by scripts/lib/z8_expectation_gate.py against the report of scripts/lib/z8_upstream_suite.py.
# Columns: name <TAB> status <TAB> min_passed <TAB> lane <TAB> reason. Measured 2026-10-30 on the tree of round 3931.
# `lane` says whether the hosted lane runs the file (`yes`) or only a person does (`no`).
# A file that does better than its row is a line to raise in the commit that made it better.

column5: all of it; the file arrived with 1.10.2 (measured on the tree of round 3976)
all of it; 4 tests are ignored upstream

measured with a process per test, as upstream's CI runs them (each scenario module installs a process-global subscriber, so one process over the file records only scenario 1): 55 of 126 pass; scenario 1 needs the client node (its ten tests time out); scenario 4 counts the registrations of its clients, which the client side does not report yet; scenarios 2, 3, 6 and 7 count the steps of regions the router does not partition by yet (gateway, south filter); orders 3 and 4 of scenario 5 take one registration more than upstream's three; each failing test waits out a minute, so a person runs it

2 tests are ignored upstream; three_node_combination lost a recipe in about one run in four until a probe stopped waiting for the lock of a lane a blocking send holds (round 4017), and passed in 8 of 8 runs after
